==Enshrined deities==
It enshrines {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iwakamutsukari-no-Mikoto}} (Takabe-no-Kami), and also {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|kk|Аматэрасу|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|mag|अमातेरासु|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu-Ōmikami}} and {{ill|Inari Ōkami|abstract|Q719665|ar|إناري|az|İnari Okami|ban|Inari (Kami)|bcl|Inari Ōkami|ca|Oinari|cs|Inari (mytologie)|da|Inari|de|Inari (Kami)|el|Ινάρι Όκαμι|es|Inari (Japón)|et|Inari (jumal)|eu|Inari Ōkami|fa|ایناری|fi|Inari (kami)|fr|Inari (divinité japonaise)|hr|Inari|hu|Inari (sintó)|hy|Ինարի Օկամի|id|Inari (Kami)|it|Inari (mitologia)|ja|稲荷神|jv|Inari (Kami)|ko|이나리노카미|mni|ꯏꯅꯔꯤ ꯑꯣꯀꯃꯤ|ne|इनारी ओकामी|nl|Inari Ōkami|no|Inari|pl|Inari (bóstwo)|pt|Inari Ōkami|ru|Инари (божество)|simple|Inari Ōkami|sl|Inari (mitologija)|sr|Инари (богиња)|sv|Inari|tok|jan sewi suli Inali|tr|Inari Ōkami|uk|Інарі (міфологія)|vi|Inari Ōkami|zh|稻荷神|qid=Q719665|lt=Inari Ōkami}}.

==History==
The origin of this shrine’s foundation is unknown, but the shrine’s history states that some descendants of the {{ill|Takahashi|ja|高橋氏|qid=Q11671376}}, descendants of Iwakamutsukari-no-Mikoto, may have moved to Awa Province, which was connected to their ancestral deity, and enshrined that deity as their ujigami. It is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} as “Takabe Shrine, {{ill|Asai District, Chiba|ja|朝夷郡|simple|Asai District, Chiba|qid=Q4803406}}, Awa Province,” but it appears to have later declined and disappeared, and its location remained unknown for a long time.

The origin of the current Takabe Shrine dates to the early {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Έντο|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|new|इदो काल|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}. In {{ill|Genna|de|Genna (Ära)|es|Genna|fa|گننا|fr|Ère Genna|id|Genna|it|Genna|ja|元和 (日本)|ko|겐나|ru|Гэнна|simple|Genna|sr|Гена|sv|Genna|tr|Genna|zh|元和 (日本)|qid=Q635245|lt=Genna}} 6 ({{ill|1620|ab|1620|af|1620|als|1620|am|1620 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1620|ar|1620|ary|1620|arz|1620|ast|1620|avk|1620|az|1620|azb|۱۶۲۰ (میلادی)|ban|1620|bcl|1620|be|1620|be_x_old|1620|bg|1620|bn|১৬২০|bpy|মারি ১৬২০|br|1620|bs|1620.|ca|1620|cdo|1620 nièng|ceb|1620|ckb|١٦٢٠|co|1620|crh|1620|cs|1620|cv|1620|cy|1620|da|1620|de|1620|diq|1620|el|1620|eml|1620|eo|1620|es|1620|et|1620|eu|1620|fa|۱۶۲۰ (میلادی)|fi|1620|fo|1620|fr|1620|frr|1620|fur|1620|fy|1620|ga|1620|gan|1620年|gcr|1620|gd|1620|gl|1620|gv|1620|he|1620|hi|१६२०|hr|1620.|ht|1620 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1620|hy|1620|hyw|1620 թուական|ia|1620|id|1620|ilo|1620|io|1620|is|1620|it|1620|ja|1620年|jv|1620|ka|1620|kaa|1620|kk|1620 жыл|kn|೧೬೨೦|ko|1620년|krc|1620 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1620|la|1620|lb|1620|lez|1620 йис|li|1620|lij|1620|lld|1620|lmo|1620|lt|1620 m.|lv|1620. gads|mai|१६२०|map_bms|1620|mdf|1620|mg|1620|mhr|1620|mi|1620|mk|1620|mr|इ.स. १६२०|mrj|1620 и|ms|1620|my|၁၆၂၀|mzn|۱۶۲۰|nap|1620|nds|1620|new|सन् १६२०|nl|1620|nn|1620|no|1620|nrm|1620|nso|1620|or|୧୬୨୦|os|1620-æм аз|pa|1620|pl|1620|pnb|1620|pt|1620|qu|1620|ro|1620|ru|1620 год|rue|1620|sa|१६२०|sah|1620|scn|1620|sd|1620ع|se|1620|sh|1620.|shn|1620|simple|1620|sk|1620|sl|1620|smn|1620|sq|1620|sr|1620|stq|1620|su|1620|sv|1620|sw|1620|szl|1620|ta|1620|tg|Соли 1620|th|พ.ศ. 2163|tk|1620|tly|1620|tr|1620|tt|1620 ел|uk|1620|ur|1620ء|uz|1620|vec|1620|vi|1620|vls|1620|wa|1620|war|1620|wuu|1620年|xmf|1620|yi|1620|zh|1620年|zh_classical|一六二〇年|zh_min_nan|1620 nî|zh_yue|1620年|qid=Q6810}}), Takagi Kichiemon discovered a wooden statue and two mirrors beneath a cherry tree, and founded a shrine called “Shinmei-sha,” using them as sacred objects. About 200 years later, it was found that one mirror bore the inscription “Miketsu no Kami, Iwakamutsukari-no-Mikoto,” and it was judged to be the sacred object of the long-lost Takabe Shrine. In {{ill|Bunsei|de|Bunsei|es|Bunsei|fa|بونسی (دوره)|fr|Ère Bunsei|ia|Bunsei|ja|文政|ko|분세이|ru|Бунсэй|simple|Bunsei|sr|Бунсеи|sv|Bunsei|tr|Bunsei|zh|文政|qid=Q1327119}} 2 ({{ill|1819|ab|1819|af|1819|als|1819|am|1819 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1819|ar|1819|ary|1819|arz|1819|ast|1819|avk|1819|az|1819|azb|۱۸۱۹ (میلادی)|ba|1819 йыл|ban|1819|bar|1819|bat_smg|1819|bcl|1819|be|1819|be_x_old|1819|bg|1819|bn|১৮১৯|bpy|মারি ১৮১৯|br|1819|bs|1819.|ca|1819|cdo|1819 nièng|ce|1819 шо|ceb|1819|ckb|١٨١٩|co|1819|crh|1819|cs|1819|csb|1819|cv|1819|cy|1819|da|1819|de|1819|diq|1819|el|1819|eml|1819|eo|1819|es|1819|et|1819|eu|1819|fa|۱۸۱۹|fi|1819|fiu_vro|1819|fo|1819|fr|1819|frp|1819|frr|1819|fur|1819|fy|1819|ga|1819|gag|1819|gan|1819年|gcr|1819|gd|1819|gl|1819|gv|1819|hak|1819-ngièn|he|1819|hi|१८१९|hif|1819|hr|1819.|hsb|1819|ht|1819 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1819|hy|1819|hyw|1819 թուական|ia|1819|id|1819|ilo|1819|io|1819|is|1819|it|1819|ja|1819年|jv|1819|ka|1819|kaa|1819|kk|1819 жыл|kn|೧೮೧೯|ko|1819년|krc|1819 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1819|kv|1819-ӧд во|la|1819|lb|1819|lez|1819 йис|li|1819|lij|1819|lmo|1819|lt|1819 m.|lv|1819. gads|mai|१८१९|map_bms|1819|mdf|1819|mg|1819|mhr|1819|mi|1819|min|1819|mk|1819|ml|1819|mn|1819 он|mr|इ.स. १८१९|mrj|1819 и|ms|1819|my|၁၈၁၉|myv|1819 ие|mzn|۱۸۱۹|nah|1819|nap|1819|nds|1819|nds_nl|1819|new|ई सं १८१९|nl|1819|nn|1819|no|1819|nrm|1819|nso|1819|oc|1819|olo|1819|or|୧୮୧୯|os|1819-æм аз|pa|1819|pap|1819|pl|1819|pnb|1819|pt|1819|qu|1819|ro|1819|ru|1819 год|rue|1819|sa|१८१९|sah|1819|scn|1819|sd|1819ع|se|1819|sh|1819.|shn|1819|si|1819|simple|1819|sk|1819|sl|1819|smn|1819|sq|1819|sr|1819|stq|1819|su|1819|sv|1819|sw|1819|szl|1819|ta|1819|te|1819|tg|Соли 1819|th|พ.ศ. 2362|tk|1819|tl|1819|tly|1819|tpi|1819|tr|1819|tt|1819 ел|ug|1819 - يىلى|uk|1819|ur|1819ء|uz|1819|vec|1819|vi|1819|vls|1819|vo|1819|wa|1819|war|1819|wuu|1819年|xmf|1819|yi|1819|zea|1819|zh|1819年|zh_min_nan|1819 nî|zh_yue|1819年|qid=Q6967}}), a petition was submitted to the Yoshida office in Kyoto for official recognition, and the shrine was renamed from Shinmei-sha to Takabe Shrine.

A divided spirit of this shrine is enshrined at the {{ill|Higeta Shoyu|ja|ヒゲタ醤油|qid=Q11329982}} factory in {{ill|Chōshi|ar|تشوشي (تشيبا)|azb|چوشی، چیبا|ce|Тёси|ceb|Chōshi-shi|de|Chōshi|eo|Ĉoŝi|es|Chōshi (Chiba)|et|Chōshi|eu|Chōshi (Chiba)|fa|چوشی، چیبا|fi|Chōshi|fr|Chōshi|gl|Chōshi|id|Chōshi, Chiba|it|Chōshi|ja|銚子市|ko|조시시|mzn|چوشی، چیبا|nl|Choshi|pl|Chōshi|pt|Choshi|ro|Chōshi|ru|Тёси|sv|Choshi|tg|Чоши|th|โชชิ|tl|Chōshi|tr|Chōshi|tt|Тёси|tum|Chōshi|uk|Тьосі (Тіба)|ur|چؤشی، چیبا|vi|Chōshi, Chiba|war|Chōshi, Chiba|zh|銚子市|zh_classical|銚子市|zh_min_nan|Tyôsi-chhī|zh_yue|銚子|qid=Q694317}} as a guardian deity of soy sauce brewing. It was enshrined there by Tanaka Naotarō (Kinchōshi), then president of the company and later author of ''Shōyu Enkakushi''. Through introductions by Tanaka Naotarō, Ishii Jibei (author of ''Nihon Ryōrihō Taizen''), and Miyake Koken of the Japanese Cuisine Research Society, the name of Takabe Shrine became known throughout Japan.
